column1: # tests/doom-core/fork/ledger.tsv — decision 0008 task 1's fork patch ledger.
# One row per defect and per opt-in patch or instrument, from the PRIMARY
# the fork's own SPINEL_LLVM_PATCHES.md and the commits themselves, not the
# historical checkpoint summary. The eleven bug-fix batches carry sixteen
# separate defects (B1..B16) plus two later batches that added no reproducer
# of their own; batch 1 alone has six. The batches are not the whole fork, so
# the opt-in patches and the analysis instruments are rows too.
# Columns are the schema docs/core/doom-stage2-fork-review.md sets, with four
# `run_status` is a PINNED MEASUREMENT, not a plan: tests/doom-core/
# fork-compat.sh runs every row that names a fixture and fails if what it
# measures disagrees with what is written here. A row with no fixture must be
# not-run or not-applicable, and every not-applicable, not-run or defer row
# must carry a reason. None of them counts as a passing execution.
# When a pin move changes what a row measures, the `run_status` is updated to
# the new measurement and the reason keeps the old one: which pin reproduced it,
# which pin did not, and what the superseded reasoning was. The row is not
# deleted and no row is added, because the ledger is one row per defect, not one
# row per measurement -- the history of a defect belongs in its own row.
# `stress` says the row is also run with SPINEL_GC_FULL_INTERVAL=1, which
# forces a collection as often as the runtime allows. The three rooting
# defects are the ones a stress run can expose that a default run may not.
